page: Vultr vcg-l40s-32c-375g-96vram is a GPU-accelerated server instance designed for intensive parallel computing workloads. It features two NVIDIA L40S GPUs based on the Ada Lovelace architecture, providing a combined 96 GB of GDDR6 VRAM. The host system is powered by an Intel Xeon 6448H processor with 32 physical cores and 32 vCPUs running at 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. It is configured with 375.0 GB of system memory, yielding approximately 11.72 GB of RAM per core, and includes 2200 GB of local NVMe SSD storage.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core and memory performance. The instance achieved a PassMark CPU score of 64,768.69 and a multi-core stress-ng score of 62,892.75, both placing in the top 25% tier. Single-core performance is moderate, with a stress-ng single-core score of 2,209.29. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, reaching 4,985.78 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and 211.9 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. The system excels in data compression and decompression, registering top-tier single-threaded gzip compression at 35.41 GB/sec and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression at 430.84 GB/sec.

The dual NVIDIA L40S GPUs deliver exceptional performance for artificial intelligence workloads. In LLM inference benchmarks using a medium 7B parameter model, the server achieved top-tier speeds of 6,275.36 tokens per second for prompt processing and 141.42 tokens per second for text generation. However, users should note that the CPU allocation is shared, which may introduce resource contention under sustained non-GPU CPU-heavy workloads. This server is highly suited for machine learning training, medium-scale LLM inference, data science pipelines, and database operations, supported by a Redis SET throughput of 70.17 million operations per second and 2,200 GB of high-speed NVMe storage.
description: Vultr vcg-l40s-32c-375g-96vram is a high-density GPU-accelerated server designed for parallel processing and machine learning workloads. It features two NVIDIA L40S GPUs with a total of 96 GB VRAM, paired with an Intel Xeon 6448H processor offering 32 physical cores and 32 vCPUs. The hardware configuration includes 375.0 GB of system memory and 2200 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. Benchmarks demonstrate strong multi-core performance, with a PassMark CPU score of 64,768.69, and top-tier LLM inference capabilities, processing 6,275.36 tokens per second on a 7B model. While the shared CPU allocation presents a potential tradeoff for sustained CPU-only tasks, the massive memory capacity and dual GPUs make this instance highly efficient for AI model training, inference, and complex data science pipelines.
